# zb_hole_split registers

<!-- Generated by hwsw/regmap.py (regmap/1) from regmap zb_hole_split 0.1.0; model sha256 46825d944e01aa7e259e1800f549f5aead9775ab43ba89cbbae211c1e6f16412.  Do not edit: change the YAML and run python3 -m hwsw.regmap gen. -->

A four-register block for the unmapped-response experiment, set to split. This block follows the house register conventions (docs/hwsw.md); the Behaviour section states each one.

Interface profile: `house` (the default: a read of a hole answers SLVERR and a write OKAY, the error-capture registers are on, byte strobes are honoured, a write of 1 to a reserved bit is ignored). No setting differs from the profile.

Settings: `unmapped=split error_capture=on partial_write=accept unaligned=ignore reserved_write=ignore wide_values=optional`.

AXI4-Lite, 32-bit registers, a 0x1000-byte window (address bits [11:2] decoded). Unmapped addresses: a read answers SLVERR with data 0 and a write answers OKAY and changes nothing. Version 0.1.0; model sha256 `46825d944e01aa7e`.

Reset is what a read returns after reset with every hardware input low.

## Access types

| Access | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RW | read/write: software writes the value; hardware sees it on an output |
| RO | read-only: the value comes from a hardware input (or is a constant); writes are ignored |
| W1C | write 1 to clear: hardware sets bits with a pulse input; software clears a bit by writing 1 to it; a set and a clear in the same clock leave the bit set (no event is lost) |
| W1S | write 1 to set: software sets bits by writing 1 (a doorbell); hardware clears them with a pulse input; a set and a clear in the same clock leave the bit set |
| W1P | write 1 to pulse: each bit written as 1 gives a one-clock pulse on an output; reads return 0 |
| RO const | read-only constant, fixed when the block is built |

## Behaviour

- **Interface profile.** `house` (the default: a read of a hole answers SLVERR and a write OKAY, the error-capture registers are on, byte strobes are honoured, a write of 1 to a reserved bit is ignored). No setting differs from the profile. The profile is chosen once per design (spec.yaml `interfaces:`) and may be overridden per block and per setting; the settings it bundles are listed in docs/hwsw.md.
- **Unmapped addresses.** An address inside this block's 0x1000-byte window that holds no register: a read answers SLVERR with data 0, and a write answers OKAY and changes nothing (split response). The read is made visible because it reports at the load on an Arm CPU (expected: a synchronous external abort); the write is quiet because a SLVERR on a posted write is expected to reach the CPU late and imprecisely, where it is hard to attribute. What an Arm CPU does with these responses is expected, not yet measured on this project's platforms (docs/hwsw.md). Addresses outside the window belong to the interconnect (an AXI crossbar answers DECERR there).
- **Error capture.** Every access to an unmapped address is recorded, whatever the response above. ERR_STATUS.STICKY (0xffc) is set by the first one since the last clear; ERR_ADDR (0xff8) then holds its word-aligned address inside the window (the address bits the block decodes) and ERR_STATUS.IS_WRITE says whether it was a write. Later bad accesses do not replace them: ERR_STATUS.COUNT counts every one, saturating at 255. Write 1 to STICKY to clear the record (STICKY and COUNT go to 0; ERR_ADDR and IS_WRITE keep their last values and are meaningful only while STICKY is 1). A bad access in the same clock as that clear is not lost: it starts the new record (STICKY 1, COUNT 1). A bad read and a bad write in the same clock count 2 and the read is the one recorded. Reads of the capture registers have no side effects. The capture raises no interrupt.
- **Reserved bits.** Bits that belong to no field read 0 and ignore writes. Write them as 0, so that a later version can give them a meaning.
- **Reads have no side effects.** Reading any register changes nothing, so a debugger or a retried read is safe. A read-modify-write must write the W1C, W1S and W1P bits as 0 (here ERR_STATUS.STICKY), or it clears, sets or pulses them: write back only the RW bits of what was read. This block has no command, doorbell or snapshot bits. A write to a read-only register is answered OKAY and ignored.
- **Same-clock priority (the house convention).** W1C bits (ERR_STATUS.STICKY): a hardware set in the same clock as a software clear wins, so the bit stays set and no event is lost.
- **Partial writes.** Byte strobes (WSTRB) are honoured on every register: a byte whose strobe is 0 keeps its value, and in it W1C, W1S and W1P bits count as 0 (nothing is cleared, set or pulsed).
- **Access width and alignment.** 32-bit registers on a 32-bit AXI4-Lite bus. AXI4-Lite has no transfer size: a CPU's byte or halfword load reads the whole word, and its store arrives as a word write with fewer strobes (see Partial writes). Address bits [1:0] are not decoded, so an unaligned address reaches the word that holds it; only bits [11:2] are decoded, so the window repeats every 0x1000 bytes. Use aligned 32-bit accesses.
- **Values wider than 32 bits.** No snapshot groups: every register is read on its own, so a value split across two registers (a HI and a LO) can tear if it changes between the two reads. Give such a value a snapshot group.
- **Reset.** `aresetn`, synchronous, active low (sampled on the rising edge of `aclk`). Every stored field takes the reset value in its table. Every register is reset.
- **Interrupt.** None: this block has no interrupt output; software polls its status.
- **Clock domain and timing.** Every field is in the `aclk` domain; hardware inputs must be synchronous to `aclk` (the block has no synchronisers). A write takes effect on the hardware in the clock its write response (BVALID) is raised. A read returns the hardware's values as they were in the clock the read address was accepted.

## ERR_STATUS (0xffc)

Error-capture flags and count.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15:8 | COUNT | RO | 0x0 | unmapped accesses since the last clear, saturating at 255 |
| 1 | IS_WRITE | RO | 0x0 | the recorded access was a write; valid while STICKY is 1 |
| 0 | STICKY | W1C | 0x0 | an unmapped access happened since the last clear; write 1 to clear (also clears COUNT) |
